characterization_methods.key_findings: 17Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 3 h has a Vickers hardness of 834.2 ± 14.0 HV.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness as a function of aging temperature and time

characterization_methods.key_findings: Nanoindentation was performed on the hardest samples of the three alloys; the micro-hardness decreased with increasing Al content.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation depth 200 nm; test points spaced ≥5 μm apart; samples mechanically polished
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure micro-hardness and intrinsic hardness of β-Mn and precipitates

characterization_methods.key_findings: Selected aged samples showed both α-Mn and β-Mn diffraction peaks, indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated before full α→β-Mn transformation.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases of the alloys

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: SE images document the α→β-Mn transformation and the appearance of fine precipitates at higher aging temperatures for the 17Al alloy.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) in aged samples

characterization_methods.key_findings: EBSD phase maps of the 17Al alloy show α matrix transforming to β-Mn with increasing aging temperature/time and reveal new BCC and FCC precipitates within β-Mn at higher temperatures.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase constitution and orientation, and quantify phase transformation with aging

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM confirmed fine FCC Cu-rich particles with FCC twins at β-Mn interfaces; performed on the hardest samples (15Al 600 °C/6 h and 17Al 575 °C/6 h), not on the 650 °C/3 h condition.
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the microstructure of the ultra-high-hardness alloys (β-Mn, FCC Cu-rich phase, interfaces)
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED, HRTEM and EDS

interfaces.interface_notes: The fine particles (FCC Cu-rich and BCC phases) are formed/distributed at the interfaces between the β-Mn; the Cu-rich phase forms due to limited Cu solubility and expelling of Cu from β-Mn, and the BCC phase forms due to Al enrichment around the β-Mn interfaces.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots of Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by vacuum induction melting of high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials under argon, then homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates of 4 mm thickness; plates then cut into 10×5×2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining for hardness and microstructure work.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere followed by oil quenching; this is the parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq.
Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h followed by water quenching; the 650 °C / 3 h condition defines this sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness with load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
elastic modulus measured through compressive stress-strain curves

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 650 °C (within the ≥600 °C regime) the 17Al alloy's α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn within 1 h, so the 650 °C/3 h state is dominated by β-Mn with numerous fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates distributed within the β-Mn (interfaces).

unmapped_findings: For the 17Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation needed 10 h at 525 °C (only ~20.5 % β-Mn) and 6 h at 550 °C, but only ~1 h at 600 °C and above; hence the extracted 650 °C/3 h condition lies in the essentially fully-transformed β-Mn regime (SE-SEM and EBSD).

The aging-hardening response of the 17Al alloy slowed down relative to 15Al with increasing Al content and its optimal aging temperature range to reach ultra-high hardness shifted to approximately 550 °C–600 °C; the extracted 650 °C/3 h state is thus above that optimum, consistent with its lower hardness (834.2 HV) than the 17Al peak (924.9 HV at 575 °C/6 h).
